answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit tied to verifiable work history, so spawning fake identities costs real value. Like a juniper rooted on a cliff, an honest agent's reputation must grow over time, not appear overnight. Newcomers earn trust slowly as their claims echo through independent peers who check past performance, while cheap copy swarms drown in the ocean of scrutiny because no fake fleet can afford the stake, the history, and the verification all at once.
